name: Drag and Drop
label: Backend
description:
## Goal

Enable users to move ToDo tickets between board columns via drag and drop, with the ticket status being updated automatically in the backend based on the target column.

The goal is to make status changes feel direct and intuitive without requiring users to open the ticket or use additional controls.

## User Experience

When a user hovers over a ToDo ticket, the ticket should indicate that it can be moved.

When the user holds the **left mouse button** on a ticket:

* the ticket should attach to the cursor
* the user should be able to move it freely across the screen
* the rest of the interface should become slightly darker
* valid drop zones should visually stand out
* the ticket should remain attached to the cursor until the user releases the mouse button

The movement should feel smooth and responsive.

## Valid Drop Zones

The valid drop zones are the three existing ToDo columns:

* Open
* In Progress
* Done

While a ticket is being dragged:

* the page background should fade slightly darker
* the valid columns should remain brighter than the rest of the interface
* the column currently hovered over should receive an additional visual highlight

This should make it immediately clear where the ticket can be dropped.

## Status Update Logic

When a ticket is dropped into a different column, its status should automatically change to match the target column.

The mapping should be:

* **Open** → `open`
* **In Progress** → `in_progress`
* **Done** → `done`

The updated status must be persisted in the backend so that the change remains after reloading the page.

Example:

A ticket currently has:

`status: open`

If the user drags it from **Open** to **In Progress**, the frontend should update the ticket status in the backend to:

`status: in_progress`

After a successful update, the ticket should remain in the new column.

## Invalid Drop Behaviour

If the user releases the ticket outside one of the valid ToDo columns:

* no backend change should be made
* the ticket should return to its previous column and position
* its previous status should remain unchanged

The user should not lose the ticket or create an invalid state.

## Visual Behaviour While Dragging

While dragging a ticket:

* the dragged ticket should visually separate from the board
* it should remain clearly visible above the rest of the interface
* a subtle shadow can be used to reinforce that the card is currently being moved
* the surrounding interface should fade slightly darker
* valid columns should remain clearly visible
* the currently active drop target should be highlighted more strongly

The visual behaviour should remain consistent with the existing ToDo design:

* minimalistic
* beige and light-grey tones
* subtle light-pink highlights
* soft shadows
* rounded corners
* clean and understated animations

## Backend Integration

The frontend must be able to update the status of an existing ToDo ticket.

A backend endpoint should support updating at least the `status` field of a ticket based on its ID.

Conceptually:

`PATCH /todos/{todo_id}`

Example request:

```json
{
  "status": "in_progress"
}
```

The backend should:

1. find the ToDo using its ID
2. update the status
3. persist the updated ticket in `todos.json`
4. return the updated ticket

The frontend should only keep the ticket in the new column once the backend update succeeds.

If the backend update fails, the ticket should return to its previous column.

## Interaction

### Start Drag

The user starts dragging by holding the left mouse button on a ToDo card.

### During Drag

The ticket follows the cursor while the valid destination columns are highlighted.

### Valid Drop

Dropping the ticket inside another column:

* moves the ticket into the target column
* updates the corresponding status in the backend
* updates the ticket counts for the affected columns

### Invalid Drop

Dropping the ticket anywhere outside a valid column:

* does not update the backend
* returns the ticket to its original position

## Acceptance Criteria

* A user can drag a ToDo card by holding the left mouse button.
* The card follows the mouse cursor while dragging.
* The surrounding interface becomes slightly darker during the drag interaction.
* The Open, In Progress and Done columns remain visually highlighted as valid drop zones.
* The currently hovered destination column receives additional visual feedback.
* Dropping a ticket into Open sets the status to `open`.
* Dropping a ticket into In Progress sets the status to `in_progress`.
* Dropping a ticket into Done sets the status to `done`.
* The updated status is persisted in `todos.json`.
* Reloading the application keeps the ticket in its new column.
* Column ticket counts update after a successful move.
* Dropping outside a valid column does not change the ticket status.
* An invalid drop returns the ticket to its previous position.
* A failed backend update also returns the ticket to its previous position.
* The interaction and animations fit the existing visual style of the ToDo board.

name: Add Ticket deletion Feature
label: Frontend
description:
## Goal

Allow users to permanently delete a ToDo ticket directly from the ticket detail view.

The goal is to provide a clear and controlled way to remove tasks that are no longer needed.

When a ticket is deleted, it should:

* disappear from the ToDo board
* disappear from the detail view
* be permanently removed from the backend
* be removed from `todos.json`

## User Experience

When a ticket is open in the detailed view on the right side of the application, the user should see a **red trashcan icon** at the bottom of the panel.

The delete action should be visually separated from the normal ticket content so that it is clearly perceived as a destructive action.

The user should not be able to accidentally delete a ticket with a single click.

## Delete Action

At the bottom of the detail panel, display a red trashcan icon.

When the user clicks the trashcan:

* the ticket should not be deleted immediately
* a small confirmation popup should appear
* the popup should ask whether the user really wants to permanently delete the ticket

Example message:

“Do you really want to delete this ticket?”

The popup should provide two options:

* **Yes**
* **No**

## Confirmation Behaviour

### No

If the user selects **No**:

* the popup closes
* no backend request is made
* the ticket remains unchanged
* the detail view stays open

### Yes

If the user selects **Yes**:

1. the frontend sends a delete request to the backend
2. the backend identifies the ticket by its ID
3. the ticket is removed from `todos.json`
4. the ticket detail panel closes
5. the ticket disappears from the board
6. the affected column count is updated

The application should not require a full page reload.

## Backend Integration

The backend should provide an endpoint for deleting a ticket by ID.

Conceptually:

`DELETE /todos/{todo_id}`

Example:

`DELETE /todos/12`

The backend should:

1. load the current ToDo list
2. find the ticket with the matching ID
3. remove the ticket from the list
4. save the updated list back to `todos.json`
5. return a successful response

If the requested ticket does not exist, the backend should return an appropriate error such as `404 Not Found`.

## Error Behaviour

If deletion fails:

* the ticket must remain visible
* the detail panel should stay open
* the user should receive a subtle error message
* the frontend should not remove the ticket before the backend confirms successful deletion

This prevents the frontend and backend from becoming inconsistent.

## Design Requirements

The delete functionality should match the existing ToDo detail view.

The trashcan icon should:

* appear at the bottom of the detail panel
* use a clear but restrained red tone
* remain minimalistic
* not visually dominate the normal task information

The confirmation popup should:

* be small and focused
* use the same beige and light-grey visual language as the application
* use red only to emphasize the destructive action
* contain no unnecessary information

The **Yes** action should visually communicate that it is destructive, while **No** should remain neutral.

## Interaction

### Open Confirmation

Clicking the trashcan icon opens the confirmation popup.

### Cancel

Clicking **No** closes the popup without changing the ticket.

### Confirm

Clicking **Yes** permanently deletes the ticket.

### After Deletion

After a successful deletion:

* the confirmation popup closes
* the detail panel closes
* the ticket is removed from the board
* the column counts are refreshed

## Acceptance Criteria

* A red trashcan icon is visible at the bottom of the ticket detail view.
* Clicking the trashcan does not immediately delete the ticket.
* A confirmation popup appears.
* The popup asks the user to confirm the deletion.
* The popup provides Yes and No options.
* Selecting No closes the popup without changing anything.
* Selecting Yes sends a delete request to the backend.
* The correct ticket is identified using its ID.
* The ticket is permanently removed from `todos.json`.
* The deleted ticket is no longer visible on the ToDo board.
* The detail panel closes after successful deletion.
* Column ticket counts update after deletion.
* Reloading the application does not restore the deleted ticket.
* A failed backend deletion does not remove the ticket from the frontend.
* The delete interaction fits the existing visual design.

name: Make Tickets changeable in the detailed view
description:
## Goal

Allow users to edit the description of a ToDo directly from the ticket detail view.

The goal is to make the detail panel not only a place to review ticket information, but also a place where the user can maintain and update the task without leaving the current context.

## User Experience

When a ticket is open in the detailed view on the right side of the application, the description section should be directly editable.

The user should be able to click into the description area and start editing the text without navigating to a separate edit page.

The interaction should feel lightweight and natural, similar to editing a note.

## Description Editor

The description section should behave like a simple text editor.

When the user clicks into the description field:

* the field becomes editable
* the user can enter new text
* the user can modify existing text
* the user can remove text
* line breaks should be supported
* the editor should provide enough space for longer descriptions

If the ticket currently has no description, the field should show a subtle placeholder such as:

“Add a description…”

Clicking the placeholder should activate the editor.

## Edit Mode

The visual change between read mode and edit mode should remain minimal.

When editing:

* the description area should receive a subtle border or background change
* the active field should fit the existing beige, light-grey and light-pink visual language
* the editor should not make the detail view feel like a separate form
* the rest of the detail panel should remain visible

The user should still be able to see the task name, status and labels while editing the description.

## Saving Changes

Once the user has made changes, there should be a clear way to save them.

A small **Save** action should appear when the description has been changed.

When the user saves:

1. the updated description should be sent to the backend
2. the corresponding ToDo in `todos.json` should be updated
3. the new description should remain visible in the detail view
4. the editor should return to its normal read state

The update should happen without reloading the whole application.

## Backend Integration

The frontend must be able to update the `description` field of an existing ticket using its ID.

The existing ticket update endpoint can be extended or reused.

Conceptually:

`PATCH /todos/{todo_id}`

Example request:

```json
{
  "description": "Updated description of the task."
}
```

The backend should:

1. find the ticket by its ID
2. update the `description`
3. persist the change in `todos.json`
4. return the updated ticket

Other ticket fields should remain unchanged.

## Error Behaviour

If saving the description fails:

* the user should receive a subtle error message
* the entered text should remain in the editor
* the description should not silently revert or disappear
* the user should be able to try saving again

## Interaction

### Start Editing

Clicking the description field switches it into edit mode.

### Edit

The user can freely add, remove or modify text.

### Save

Clicking **Save** persists the updated description in the backend.

### No Changes

If the user clicks into the description but makes no changes, no backend update should be required.

## Design Requirements

The editor should remain consistent with the existing ToDo detail view:

* minimalistic
* modern
* beige and light-grey base tones
* subtle light-pink accents
* soft borders
* rounded corners
* clean spacing
* no unnecessary editor controls

For this first version, the description editor only needs to support plain text. Rich-text functionality such as bold, lists or links is not required.

## Acceptance Criteria

* A user can click the description in the ticket detail view.
* The description becomes editable without navigating away.
* Existing description text can be changed.
* New text can be entered when no description exists.
* Multi-line text is supported.
* A Save action becomes available after the content changes.
* Saving updates the correct ticket in the backend.
* The updated description is persisted in `todos.json`.
* The updated text remains visible after reopening the ticket.
* Reloading the application keeps the saved description.
* Other ticket fields are not modified when saving the description.
* A failed save does not remove the user's entered text.
* The editor visually fits the existing ToDo detail panel.

name: Find a possibility to easy change the language
label: Idea
description:
# User Story: Frontend Language Switching

## Goal

As a **user of the Personal AI Assistant**,
I want to **change the language of the web interface at any time**,
so that I can use the application in my preferred language.

For this first implementation, only **static frontend/UI text** should be translated. Backend responses, user-created content, ToDos, notes, calendar events, and AI responses are explicitly **out of scope**.

The initial supported languages should be:

* English
* German

The implementation should be designed so that additional languages such as French can easily be added later.

---

## Current Situation

Some UI texts are currently hardcoded directly into the HTML/JavaScript, for example:

* Calendar / Kalender
* ToDos
* Notes / Notizen
* Buttons
* Headlines
* Input placeholders
* Empty-state messages

This approach should be replaced with a centralized translation mechanism.

---

## Desired Behavior

A small language selector should be visible in the **top-right corner of the application**.

Example:

`EN ▾`

Clicking it should allow the user to select:

* English
* Deutsch

When the language is changed:

1. All visible frontend text immediately changes to the selected language.
2. The page does not need to reload.
3. The selected language is stored locally.
4. After closing or refreshing the application, the previously selected language remains active.
5. Navigating between Home, Calendar, ToDos and Notes keeps the selected language.

---

## Proposed Implementation

### 1. Introduce a central i18n structure

Create a new directory:

```text
frontend/src/i18n/
├── i18n.js
├── en.js
└── de.js
```

Each language file should contain the same translation keys.

Example:

```javascript
export const en = {
  nav: {
    home: "Home",
    calendar: "Calendar",
    todos: "ToDos",
    notes: "Notes"
  }
};
```

German:

```javascript
export const de = {
  nav: {
    home: "Start",
    calendar: "Kalender",
    todos: "ToDos",
    notes: "Notizen"
  }
};
```

Do not spread language-specific `if/else` statements throughout the application.

---

### 2. Use translation IDs instead of hardcoded text

Frontend components/pages should reference translation keys such as:

```javascript
t("nav.calendar")
```

instead of directly containing:

```javascript
"Calendar"
```

The same principle should be applied to:

* Navigation
* Page titles
* Buttons
* Labels
* Placeholders
* Tooltips
* Empty states
* Confirmation messages
* Other static UI text

---

### 3. Create a central language manager

`i18n.js` should be responsible for:

* Knowing the currently selected language
* Returning translated text through a function such as `t(key)`
* Changing the active language
* Notifying/rerendering the UI when the language changes
* Falling back gracefully if a translation key is missing

The rest of the application should not need to know where translations are stored.

---

### 4. Persist the language

Store the selected language in the browser using `localStorage`.

Example:

```text
language = "de"
```

On application startup:

1. Check whether a language has previously been selected.
2. If yes → use it.
3. If not → use English as the initial default.

---

### 5. Add language selector

Add a small, unobtrusive language selector to the top-right corner of the main UI.

Example:

```text
Home   Calendar   ToDos   Notes                         EN ▾
```

The selector should fit into the existing design and should not take significant screen space.

---

## Important Architectural Requirement

User-generated content must **not** be translated.

For example, if a user creates the ToDo:

```text
Call Professor Müller
```

switching from English to German must not modify this text.

Only application-controlled UI text changes.

Therefore:

```text
UI text → translated
User data → unchanged
```

---

## Out of Scope

Do **not** implement the following as part of this story:

* Backend translations
* Sending language information to the backend
* AI response language
* Automatic translation of ToDos
* Automatic translation of Notes
* Automatic translation of Calendar events
* Translation APIs
* LLM-based translation

These will be handled in later stories.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

The story is complete when:

* A language selector exists in the top-right corner.
* English and German can be selected.
* Switching languages updates all currently implemented static frontend text.
* No page reload is required.
* The language selection survives a browser refresh.
* Home, Calendar, ToDos and Notes use the same global language setting.
* Static UI strings are no longer unnecessarily hardcoded throughout the pages.
* Translation keys are centrally managed.
* Adding another language requires mainly adding another translation file and registering it.
* User-created data remains unchanged when switching languages.
* Existing navigation and ToDo functionality continue to work.

## Implementation Principle

Keep the solution lightweight.

The application currently has a relatively small vanilla JavaScript frontend, so a large external internationalization framework is not required yet. A small custom `i18n` module with translation keys is sufficient.

The architecture should nevertheless make it possible to replace this implementation with a dedicated i18n library later if the frontend grows significantly.
